content:
incident-bot: Pager fired -> severity: P1 | service: limiter-service | symptom: sudden spike in 429s across multiple regions. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/limiter-anomaly

pagerduty: Page: RateLimiter - Excess 429s (Triggered by service: limiter-service). Details: 200+ 429/sec for last 60s, increased error budget use. Escalation: oncall -> sre -> eng-runtime.

sam: acked. I'm on the pager. starting timeline investigation now.

priya: looking at metrics — cluster-limiter metrics show token-bucket drop to near-zero capacity at 17:12 UTC, simultaneous with a config push to quota-mapping-service at 17:11. could be config ripple.

jordan: fyi I see many tenants suddenly mapped to a global quota id: "global-free-tier" in the new mapping. that would collapse per-tenant limits into a shared bucket -> cascade.

sam: can we confirm deploy history? who pushed quota-mapping at ~17:11? @ops-manager-ken or @lydia?

lydia: that was an automated rollout from the ops pipeline (PR #5123). I approved canary earlier. I didn't see alerts in staging.

miguel: CS reporting customers A and B showing 429s and degraded UI. Miguel, can you collect request ids?

miguel: sending sample request ids in case notes: req_abc123, req_def456. also customers report timeouts after retries.

priya: grabbing logs from mapping service:
```
2026-03-14T17:11:04Z INFO apply_mapping batch=1024 mappings_applied=1024 override=false
2026-03-14T17:11:05Z WARN mapping_module: duplicate_key detected tenant_id=acct_xxx mapped_to=global-free-tier
```

jordan: suggested mitigation options: 1) rollback quota-mapping rollout to previous tag (safe path) 2) apply emergency per-tenant override via admin API 3) route traffic to secondary limiter pool that still has correct mapping.

sam: rolling back mapping rollout now. executing:
```
kubectl -n infra rollout undo deploy/quota-mapping-service --to-revision=210
```

sam: rollback started. notifying PD to pause escalations.

pagerduty: Note: Pager escalations paused by ack from sam.

priya: while rollback streams, enabling secondary limiter route:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://control-plane.internal/routing/route -d '{"service":"limiter-service","target":"limiter-pool-b","weight":100}'
```

jordan: scaling limiter replicas as temporary measure:
```
kubectl scale deployment limiter --replicas=8 -n inference
```

lydia: notifying product and CS: product @lydia, CS @miguel — impacted customers list?

miguel: preliminary list: acct-A (high), acct-B (medium), acct-legacy-7 (low). I'll open support tickets and apply priority notifications.

sam: rollback completed at 17:18 UTC. mapping-service logs show previous mapping restored. limter metrics trending down for 429s.

priya: metrics update: 429/sec dropped from 230 -> 12 over 6 minutes. error budget stabilizing. link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/limiter/429s?from=now-15m

jordan: traffic routing reverted back to primary by control-plane. limiter replicas left at 8 for safety.

ops-manager-ken: good containment. start a customer-impact note and block downtime window for postmortem.

sam: marking incident as mitigated at 17:24 UTC. leaving watch for 1h.

lydia: can someone own the postmortem? I nominate @priya to lead + @jordan for remediation plan.

priya: happy to own postmortem. I'll include follow-ups: stricter canary gating, add invariant test to mapping pipeline to reject duplicate/global mapping, and auto-rollback on spike detection.

miguel: CS will send templated apology and incident summary to impacted customers after final postmortem draft.

sam: closing notes: root cause: automated rollout of quota-mapping created unintended duplicate mapping to a shared global quota id, causing limiter token collapse and cascade 429s. immediate mitigations: rollback, reroute, scale. Long term: tighter pipeline checks + monitoring.

pagerduty: Incident resolved (ack closed). Please file postmortem and link here.

incident-bot: Reminder — create incident ticket: https://redwood.internal/incidents/create?ts=2003456789&owner=priya

sam: assigning follow-up tasks in ops board. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
